chunks: Have control over your sense of prestige (or self-esteem),
and the outburst of your anger, the might of your arm, and the sharpness of your tongue.
Guard against all this by avoiding haste and by delaying severe action,
till your anger subsides and you regain your self-control.
You cannot withhold yourself from this unless you bear in mind that you have to return to Allāh.
ai.seo_question: How does one control anger and self according to Imam Ali's instructions to Malik al-Ashtar?
ai.summary: This directive, part of the foundational political ethics in Nahj al-Balagha, emphasizes that true governance requires internal mastery over one's ego (nafs) and impulses before exercising external authority. Imam Ali links this self-discipline to the concept of *muraqaba* (awareness of God), suggesting that frequent contemplation of the Hereafter (*al-Ma'ad*) serves as the spiritual anchor for maintaining justice and restraint in leadership.
